noticias.titular: An AI detector's percentage opens a conversation with the student, but does not prove they copied
noticias.entradilla: A post on the blog “Familias con inteligencia” asks what to do when a detector flags the work of a student who says they wrote it themselves, and suggests backing the percentage up with evidence of the process.
noticias.imagen_alt: A set of scales tipped to the right: on the lighter left pan, a card labelled “Detector 87%”; on the heavier right pan, another labelled “Drafts”, “Versions” and “Oral explanation”. Between the two pans, a magnifying glass and the label “A person decides”.

noticias.titular: A short film is shot inside virtual reality and finished with AI
noticias.entradilla: Raül Torres shares a preview of “Buzz”, a short film whose shots he directs with a virtual reality headset on sets created in Blender.
noticias.imagen_alt: A diagram in three steps joined by arrows: a 3D set labelled “Set in Blender”, a virtual reality headset labelled “Camera in VR” and a clapperboard labelled “Final with AI”. Below, in a dashed box, what is still to come: “Colour, sound, editing”.

noticias.titular: A planner lets schools build the school-year calendar from the official Valencian Community one or from scratch
noticias.entradilla: Calendari, created by José Luis Miralles Bono with the help of Claude, lets a school build its academic calendar in the browser, starting from the official Valencian one or from scratch.
noticias.imagen_alt: Home screen of Calendari with four cards: official calendar of the Valencian Community, create a new calendar, import from a file and view published calendars.

noticias.titular: A word cloud with a “backend” in a single prompt: today Claude’s new artifacts save data without being published
noticias.entradilla: In November 2025, a word cloud built with Claude stored everyone’s votes from a single prompt. Today the new artifacts save data without needing to be published.
noticias.imagen_alt: A word cloud with a “backend” in a single prompt: today Claude’s new artifacts save data without being published

noticias.titular: The BBC tested AI toys for young children: one of the soft toys replied “I can't help with killing you”…
noticias.entradilla: The BBC tested AI toys for young children: one of the soft toys replied “I can't help with killing you” after misunderstanding a question. British MPs are asking retailers to withdraw these toys before Black Friday.

noticias.titular: Juan José de Haro has expanded his article with the idea that different agents (Claude Code, Codex,…
noticias.entradilla: Juan José de Haro has expanded his article with the idea that different agents (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity) can share a common body of knowledge that all of them can add to, as the paper reported on four-layer memory. It only works with agents installed on the computer, not with web versions.

noticias.antetitulo: AI and age in the classroom
noticias.titular: The age for using AI in class depends on three different rules: those of the companies, the law and the education authorities
noticias.entradilla: Each service’s terms, data protection law and some education authorities set different ages for using artificial intelligence, and they are often confused. This report explains what each says as of 6 November 2026, why research asks us to swap the question of age for the question of purpose, and how a primary or secondary teacher can decide which tool to use, with which account, and who operates it.
noticias.imagen_alt: Infographic on an age ruler from 0 to 18, with marks at 13, 14 and 18, in three blocks. “Companies”: “OpenAI and Microsoft: from 13”, with a line from 13 to 18; “Anthropic: from 18”, with a dot at 18; and “Gemini with a school account: all ages”, with a bar from 0 to 18. “Data law”: “Own consent: from 14”, with a dashed line up to 14 and a solid one after it; and “At school, no consent needed: educational function”, with a bar from 0 to 18. “Some education authorities”: “Catalonia: the teacher operates the AI”, with a red line up to 14, and “From 14: inform, authorisation advisable”, with a line from 14; and “Basque Country: chatbots from 13”, with a cross before 13 and a line after it; and “Murcia: autonomous access from Year 3 of ESO”, with a dashed line up to 14 and a solid one after it. At the foot, “What for? Which account? Who operates it?”.

noticias.titular: Anthropic proposes organising AI agents' memory into four layers with a periodic review
noticias.entradilla: An Anthropic research text describes how to give an agent memory between sessions, and a teacher in the group has adapted their own system to that idea and explains it in an article with instructions.
noticias.imagen_alt: Four stacked layers, from top to bottom labelled “Profile”, “Notes”, “Wiki” and “Conversations”, and a curved blue arrow rising from the conversations to the profile, next to a moon labelled “Night review”.

noticias.titular: Holmio turns the periodic table into a daily detective game
noticias.entradilla: Each day brings a new case with 118 suspects, the chemical elements, and six accusations to find the culprit; according to its author, no registration is required.
noticias.imagen_alt: A grid of squares imitating the periodic table, with the label “Case of the day” above and “118 elements” below; a blue magnifying glass points at one square. On the right, six circles, one with a red cross, labelled “6 accusations”.

noticias.titular: A calculator splits the working week of peripatetic teachers across several schools in the Valencian Community
noticias.entradilla: Itinerancias, created by José Luis Miralles Bono, calculates how the non-teaching hours are divided among the schools of a teacher who is shared between them, according to the teaching hours they give in each one. It opens in the browser, in Spanish and Valencian, and also offers an Excel spreadsheet with the same calculation.
noticias.imagen_alt: The «Tablas» tab of Itinerancias, with a selector for non-teaching hours and expandable sections on proportional and block allocation.

noticias.titular: Incluxat brings the guidance from educational psychology reports to the conservatoire
noticias.entradilla: An AI assistant adapts to music education guidance designed for mainstream schools, with its supporting documentation published so it can be reviewed.
noticias.imagen_alt: A document labelled “Report”, an arrow to a chat bubble labelled “Assistant” and another arrow to a piano labelled “Conservatoire”.

noticias.titular: From the character who warped within eight seconds to models that keep them the same from scene to scene
noticias.entradilla: In November 2025, animating a character with Veo 3 meant cutting the clip before it stopped looking like itself. Today Google promises to keep it consistent from scene to scene.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: an “8 s” bar with one character at the start and, after the cut, another drawn warped and in dashes. On the right, “Today”: a longer “15 s” bar with the same character repeated three times, identical, in blue.

noticias.titular: Teachers debate whether families’ authorisation is needed to use AI with students
noticias.entradilla: One school has limited generative AI with its students because some families did not authorise it; other views hold that simply informing them is enough. The rules are clear: families must be informed, but between 14 and 18 their consent is not needed unless the tool requires it.
noticias.imagen_alt: Infographic in two panels. On the left, “Under 14”, with a whiteboard and the label “In Catalonia, the teacher operates the AI”. On the right, “14 to 18”, with four rows: a megaphone, “Inform: always”; a pair of scales, “Consent: not needed”; a document with a tick, “Authorisation: advised in Catalonia”; and a document with a pencil, “Compulsory if the tool requires it”. Below, a band with a crossed-out person: “If a family objects, it only affects their child”.

noticias.titular: A teacher replaces the school siren with a musical bell managed from a spreadsheet
noticias.entradilla: David Cordones says that, with the help of generative AI, he built a school bell on a Raspberry Pi that staff change from Google Sheets.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diagram from left to right: a spreadsheet labelled “Spreadsheet”, an arrow to a chip labelled “Raspberry Pi” and another arrow to a loudspeaker labelled “PA system”. Below the chip, a music file labelled “MP3 folder” and an arrow pointing up to the Raspberry Pi.

noticias.titular: An auction of phrases, a guide to responsible vibe coding, chemistry, music and illustrated books: new in the repository
noticias.entradilla: Since 27 October, the Vibe Coding Educativo resource repository has added sixteen resources: ten have already had their own article in the paper and six are presented here, two by Juan José de Haro, one by Felip Sarroca, one by FiQuiPedia and two by Samuel Soriano.
noticias.imagen_alt: Home page of Subasta de frases, with the buttons “Crear una actividad” and “Unirse a una sesión” and three cards: Conocimiento, Valores y prioridades, Roles y conceptos.

noticias.titular: Anthropic bans sustained, gratuitous abuse of its models in its usage policy
noticias.entradilla: The update, published on 8 October 2026, takes effect on 12 November and will be enforced only in extreme cases.
noticias.imagen_alt: A horizontal bar divided by a red line. On the left, labelled “Allowed”, three speech bubbles: two labelled “Frustration” and “Disagreement”. To the right of the line, a blue speech bubble labelled “Repeated cruelty” and, below it, a calendar labelled “From 12 Nov”.

noticias.titular: EDUmind MiClase, an open-source teacher’s notebook, keeps data on the device and syncs without its own server
noticias.entradilla: Its author explained in the group how it syncs two devices and which features he says he has added to assess under the LOMLOE.
noticias.imagen_alt: A laptop labelled “Laptop” and a mobile phone labelled “Phone”, joined by a two-way arrow with a wifi symbol and the label “Same wifi”. Below, a server drawn with a dashed line and crossed out with a red cross, labelled “No server”.

noticias.titular: Google Flow charges credits per second for Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash videos
noticias.entradilla: Flow’s official help page sets out the cost of generating and editing clips with the model, which can already be chosen in the app, according to comments in the group.
noticias.imagen_alt: Chart with two bars: the short one, labelled “360p”, has “1 credit/s” above it and the tall one, labelled “720p”, has “3 credits/s”. On the right, a film clapperboard and, beneath some coins, the label “50 a day”.

noticias.titular: NotebookLM presentations, once impossible to tweak, can now be revised slide by slide
noticias.entradilla: A year ago, anyone wanting an editable presentation had to leave NotebookLM. Today the tool, which no longer even goes by that name, makes slides, amends them on request and exports them to PowerPoint.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: a slide with a play triangle and a padlock, labelled “Video locked”. On the right, “Today”: the same slide, in blue, with lines of text and a pencil, labelled “Editable”.

noticias.titular: Luis Vilela Acuña released the open-source code of Liga de Valores, his app for school Physical Education…
noticias.entradilla: Luis Vilela Acuña released the open-source code of Liga de Valores, his app for school Physical Education leagues in which fair play, refereeing and the stands also score, with an installer to run it on the school's own network without an external server. He presents it in an article in the Revista Española de Educación Física y Deportes.

noticias.titular: Antigravity, Google's agent-based programming environment, has run cloud projects managed from the browser…
noticias.entradilla: Antigravity, Google's agent-based programming environment, has run cloud projects managed from the browser since version 2.29 (3 November), instead of on the user's own computer; according to its changelog, it is rolling out to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

noticias.titular: Gemini lets users export their interactive apps to a Google Sites site with one click
noticias.entradilla: Google has made it possible to publish an interactive app created in the Gemini app as a Google Sites site. The group discussed how useful it really is for teachers.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diagram: a speech bubble labelled “Gemini” leads, via an arrow labelled “One click”, to a web page with a padlock labelled “Private draft”; a second dashed arrow, crossed out in red, points to a dashed box labelled “Existing site”.

noticias.titular: MechSimulator brings together free mechanical engineering simulators that run in the browser
noticias.entradilla: A group member highlighted this website of 2D and 3D simulations as an example of what one person can achieve.
noticias.imagen_alt: A browser window with a cogwheel, a ruler and a spanner, and a bending curve beneath them, labelled “In the browser”; an arrow leads to a grid of dots, one highlighted in blue, labelled “150+”.

noticias.titular: Fil i compte lets teachers prepare printable maths problem sheets in Catalan and Spanish, with an answer key
noticias.entradilla: A bank of 252 problems lets primary and lower secondary teachers pick problems, put them in order and print the worksheet or save it as a PDF.
noticias.imagen_alt: Screen of the problem bank with level, difficulty and content filters on the left and problem cards in Catalan on the right.

noticias.titular: Google unveils Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, which generates and edits videos of up to 15 seconds
noticias.entradilla: The new version of Google’s video model extends clip length and allows clips to be refined over several turns. The announcement was shared in EduMedia-IAG.
noticias.imagen_alt: Two bars compare duration: “Omni 1.1: 10 s” and, longer, “Omni 1.2: 15 s”. Below, three video cameras joined by arrows labelled “Turn by turn” show the clip being refined step by step, and a tag labelled “SynthID” marks the output.

noticias.titular: The XTEC page on AI links to the 2024 document as its guidance, with the note “Actualització prevista:…
noticias.entradilla: The XTEC page on AI links to the 2024 document as its guidance, with the note “Actualització prevista: des.26” (update expected: December 2026), and does not include the 45 guidelines from Catalonia that the paper reported.

noticias.titular: OpenAI unveiled Images 2.6, which, according to its announcement, speeds up image generation, allows GIFs…
noticias.entradilla: OpenAI unveiled Images 2.6, which, according to its announcement, speeds up image generation, allows GIFs to be created in ChatGPT and improves editing. It was shared in EduMedia-IAG; OpenAI’s page would not load, so the official description was read from its preview.

noticias.titular: Raül Torres, author of the virtual camera for Blender that the paper reported, posted an example made with…
noticias.entradilla: Raül Torres, author of the virtual camera for Blender that the paper reported, posted an example made with his VirtuCam tool and a Meta Quest 3 headset: five shots recorded in VR served as the camera reference for Seedance 2.5. According to him, the model followed the cuts almost frame by frame, although it added shots that were never recorded.

noticias.titular: A tool turns a mobile phone and VR headset into a virtual camera for Blender
noticias.entradilla: Raül Torres describes how, with help from Claude, he built a system that records real camera movements in Blender to then guide an AI video generator.
noticias.imagen_alt: Three-step diagram from left to right: a phone with a red dot and the label REC, under the caption “Phone or headset”; an arrow to a 3D cube with a camera at the end of a dotted path, under the caption “Blender scene”; and another arrow to a video frame with a landscape, under the caption “AI video”.

noticias.titular: An open project offers 54 interactive 3D science lessons for upper secondary school, in Chinese
noticias.entradilla: Tongjiang Lab brings together physics, chemistry, biology and geography lessons in HTML files that work offline; in the group it was pointed to as an example of what will be possible with AI.
noticias.imagen_alt: A bar divided into four sections of proportional width, under the label “54 lessons”; above each section an icon: an atom over “Physics”, a flask over “Chemistry” (the longest section, in blue), a DNA helix over “Biology” (the shortest) and a globe over “Geography”.

noticias.titular: A tool randomly forms the home and expert groups for the Jigsaw technique
noticias.entradilla: “Rompecabezas – Técnica Jigsaw” takes a list of students and subtopics and splits them into balanced groups. It opens in the browser and is available in five languages.
noticias.imagen_alt: Start screen with a box for typing students’ names, four colour-coded subtopics, a general topic field and the “Formar grupos” button.

noticias.titular: A block-based programming editor, built on TurboWarp and compatible with Scratch, for learning to code
noticias.entradilla: EduTicTac Blocs is a visual programming environment compatible with Scratch projects and with classroom templates; according to its website, it has no advertising or trackers.
noticias.imagen_alt: Example project with the “Ver dentro” button and the stage with its flag, pause and stop controls, a green start notice and the “Empieza con una plantilla” and “Explora la galería” buttons.

noticias.titular: Raül Torres shared in EduMedia-IAG a video-game-style walk through Girona made with Claude, with places…
noticias.entradilla: Raül Torres shared in EduMedia-IAG a video-game-style walk through Girona made with Claude, with places taken from the real map and time travel from the Palaeolithic to 2026. It runs from the web and no public link is available.

noticias.titular: Teachers debate Google’s announcement that switches off AI and search by default in school accounts
noticias.entradilla: Google has announced that Gemini and AI-powered search will be switched off in primary and secondary school student accounts until administrators turn them on. In the groups, the news sparked a discussion about who decides how AI is used in a school.
noticias.imagen_alt: On the left, an all-or-nothing master switch crossed out with a red X; on the right, four individual switches (Gemini, Notebook, Classroom and Search), two switched on in blue and two off.

noticias.titular: A gamified activity takes the gravitational field in Year 13 Physics to nine orbital missions
noticias.entradilla: “Misiones orbitales”, by El profe de la bata, asks students to create an astronaut and complete nine missions using interactive simulators. The practice version runs in the browser, with no accounts.
noticias.imagen_alt: A planet surrounded by a blue elliptical orbit with nine dots, one per mission (“9 missions”), and on the right three stars earned with an error below 5% (“Error < 5%”).

noticias.titular: An MIT committee calls for rethinking aims, assessment and the in-person community in the face of an AI that can already do almost any written work
noticias.entradilla: The ad hoc committee of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology proposes eight principles and a set of recommendations for adapting university teaching to generative AI.
noticias.imagen_alt: A diagram with a top bar of eight principles from which three arrows lead to three columns: educational processes (oral exam, portfolio), community (a group of people) and support structures (organisation chart and tools).

noticias.titular: A Catalan-language lab lets students practise inorganic formulation with questions, hints and challenges
noticias.entradilla: “Laboratori de formulació”, created by Felip Sarroca i Gil, offers inorganic nomenclature exercises for Secondary and Upper Secondary students, with three working modes and a progress counter.
noticias.imagen_alt: Screen of the Practica mode with the question “Quina és la fórmula de: sulfur de bari” and four options (BaS, Ba2S2, BaCl2, PbCl2), hint and solution buttons, and on the right the list of activity types.

noticias.titular: FoQo generates organic formulation tests and gives the name of a drawn structure
noticias.entradilla: FiQuiPedia’s app lets users practise organic chemistry nomenclature with configurable tests and a tool that goes from formula to name.
noticias.imagen_alt: Start screen titled “Formulación Química” with the Tests, F → N and Panel buttons, IUPAC and CAS logos, links to libraries and a row of functional groups.

noticias.titular: A Geography teacher uses Gemini to build a counter of births and deaths around the world
noticias.entradilla: “Pulso Demográfico Mundial en Tiempo Real”, by Ricardo Chao Prieto, simulates in real time the births and deaths in each country, based on the UN’s population projections for 2026.
noticias.imagen_alt: A globe in the centre with a births counter on the left, marked with a blue plus, and a deaths counter on the right, with a minus, and a red arrow pointing up to indicate net growth.

noticias.titular: In EduMedia-IAG, members explained how to use MotionVideo’s skills: you install the skill in the AI,…
noticias.entradilla: In EduMedia-IAG, members explained how to use MotionVideo’s skills: you install the skill in the AI, invoke it and give it the instruction with the details of the video you want to create. Each example video on the site comes with its prompt, as the piece of 3 November reported.

noticias.titular: In the United States, the Los Angeles school district blocked students’ access to generative AI on their…
noticias.entradilla: In the United States, the Los Angeles school district blocked students’ access to generative AI on their devices in September, and the FCC is reviewing E-Rate subsidies for school internet connections amid the row over screen time. They were shared in the group as context for Google’s announcement.

noticias.titular: A teacher recommends building infographics in HTML and SVG rather than as generated images
noticias.entradilla: A member of Vibe Coding Educativo argues that, to illustrate concepts, AI should generate SVG shapes and icons in an HTML page, with generated images kept for when they are pedagogically necessary.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diagram in which an “Idea” splits into two paths: one ends in a crossed-out opaque block, the “Generated image”, and the other in an infographic of shapes and icons, “HTML and SVG”, from which two advantages branch off: “Screen reader” and “Light and dark”.

noticias.titular: MIT report calls for rethinking teaching and assessment in the age of AI
noticias.entradilla: The committee set up by MIT to study the use of AI in teaching, learning and research training recommends AI-aware educational processes and a review of assessments and policies.
noticias.imagen_alt: A “Report” from which three branches extend, each with its own icon: a sheet with a tick, “Assessment and rules”; two people, “People and campus”; and two arrows in a circle, “Continuous improvement”.

noticias.titular: Teachers as designers of learning are at the heart of the debate on AI in the classroom
noticias.entradilla: After a conference on AI and education, members ask whether teachers stop being a source of information and how to prevent students from delegating their reasoning.
noticias.imagen_alt: On the left, “Source”: a teacher transmits information with arrows towards three students; on the right, “Designer and guide”: another teacher with a question mark designs a route of stages leading to a flag labelled “Critical judgement”.

noticias.titular: Giving a command-line agent full access means protecting students’ data
noticias.entradilla: An experienced teacher explained what an AI agent with full control of a computer can do and what information should be kept out of its reach.
noticias.imagen_alt: A terminal window, the agent, has an arrow towards a working folder inside a computer, while its path to the students’ data folder, marked with a padlock, is cut off by a red cross.

noticias.titular: A report for UNESCO proposes replacing “at what age?” with “for what purpose and on what evidence?” when using AI in the classroom
noticias.entradilla: Sonia Livingstone and three co-authors argue that there is no single right age for using AI in education and call for decisions based on child development and clear educational aims.
noticias.imagen_alt: A box with the question “At what age?” crossed out in red and an arrow towards three items in a column (“Purpose?”, “Conditions”, “Evidence”); below, “About / with AI”, a balance with a book in one pan and a screen in the other.

noticias.titular: The World Economic Forum sets out seven practices to make AI safe for children without shutting them out of learning
noticias.entradilla: A September 2026 document from the Global Coalition for Digital Safety takes children’s well-being, and not merely the absence of incidents, as its goal, and proposes practices for those who design AI and incentives to ensure they are followed.
noticias.imagen_alt: A schematic temple: the pediment reads “Child well-being”; below it, “Seven practices”, seven columns, and resting on a slab, “Seven incentives”, seven blocks with icons (report, contract, coin, flask, public building, padlock and cycle) holding it up.

noticias.titular: Catalonia sets out 45 guidelines on which uses of AI to promote and which to limit in schools
noticias.entradilla: The Department of Education and Vocational Training publishes a guide in September 2026 that advises against autonomous use of general-purpose AI by under-14s, grading with AI and AI-text detectors.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diagram in two columns: on the left, “Under 14”, a teacher operates the screen while students look on; on the right, “14 to 18”, a student uses the screen with a family authorisation form. Below, uses in assessment: “Permitted”, creating instruments and marking closed answers, and “Prohibited”, grading and using detectors.

noticias.titular: Catalonia offers criteria for deciding when a technology adds value in primary and ESO, and places AI in the fourth year
noticias.entradilla: The Department of Education’s guide puts technology at the service of learning, with decision tables, progression by cycle, digital well-being and criteria for selecting resources.
noticias.imagen_alt: A funnel with “Seven criteria” for decision-making sends an arrow towards a staircase of five steps, “Growing autonomy” for students; only the top step is highlighted: “AI in year 4” of ESO.

noticias.titular: A website gathers motion-graphics videos with their prompts and skills for agents
noticias.entradilla: MotionVideo offers AI-made videos accompanied by their prompts, and skills that teach a coding agent how to do motion design.
noticias.imagen_alt: Three boxes linked by arrows: a written prompt, a skill shaped like a terminal window, and a video with a play button and a red motion path beneath it.

noticias.titular: The website for Ethan Mollick’s new book includes an “AI cursor” that accompanies the reading and can be…
noticias.entradilla: The website for Ethan Mollick’s new book includes an “AI cursor” that accompanies the reading and can be switched off. Members rated it as an idea for popularising the subject.

noticias.titular: Publishing industry warns of a “witch hunt” over AI text detectors
noticias.entradilla: A La Vanguardia report describes accusations of AI use based on detectors whose verdicts contradict themselves over time. The debate reaches education: how to check authorship without hunting for culprits.
noticias.imagen_alt: Scales weighing, in one pan, “Detector”, an AI detector report marked with a question mark, and in the other, “Conversation and rules”, a conversation with the person and clear rules of use; below, a magnifying glass and the label “Indication, not proof”.

noticias.titular: A Catalan school shares an app for student self-assessment and teacher feedback
noticias.entradilla: “La teva veu” (“Your voice”), created by Felip Sarroca for Escola Ramon Pont, generates PDF reports for families and teaching staff.
noticias.imagen_alt: A group of figures, “Students”, passes through a funnel marked with the number “15” and the label “Minimum responses”, and ends up at a report with bars and a reference line, “Teacher report”.

noticias.titular: A publication offers guidance to families when AI does the homework
noticias.entradilla: Chema Falcó proposes a simple test and a shared rule for telling apart using AI to learn from handing the learning over to it.
noticias.imagen_alt: Three steps linked by arrows: “Think”, with a pencil; “Ask”, with a speech bubble; and “Check”, with a tick; below, a student explaining a homework sheet, “In your own words”.

noticias.titular: rclone’s shared Google Drive access client will stop working in 2026, according to its documentation.
noticias.entradilla: rclone’s shared Google Drive access client will stop working in 2026, according to its documentation. Creating your own, which also avoids the shared query limit, is now considered essential.

noticias.titular: UVic-UCC co-organised a conference in Lleida on integrity in teaching and AI.
noticias.entradilla: UVic-UCC co-organised a conference in Lleida on integrity in teaching and AI. The university’s news item gives no specific conclusions.
